entities.summary:
Phayllos of Croton was a renowned ancient Greek athlete and naval commander from Croton in southern Italy, who played a pivotal role in the Battle of Salamis. Born into a prominent family, Phayllos was trained in athletics and warfare from a young age, honing his skills under the guidance of renowned coaches. His exceptional abilities led to his appointment as commander of a trireme, which he outfitted and commanded against the Persian Empire, contributing significantly to the Greek victory at Salamis.

Phayllos' legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he is credited with helping to establish the city of Croton as a major center for athletic training and naval warfare. His son, Phayllos Jr., would go on to become a prominent athlete in his own right, further cementing the family's reputation as leaders in the field.

The impact of Phayllos' actions can still be felt today, as the Battle of Salamis marked a significant turning point in the Greco-Persian Wars, ultimately leading to the decline of the Persian Empire and the rise of Greece as a dominant power in the ancient world.

In conclusion, Phayllos of Croton was a hero of the ancient world, whose remarkable achievements in athletics and naval warfare have left an indelible mark on history.
